newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee dips as RBI resumes buying forward dlr.
newsitem.headline: India rupee dips as RBI resumes buying forward dlr.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) resumed its dollar purchase from the inter-bank foreign exchange market on Wednesday, dealers said.
RBI's dollar outright purchases of June to August dollars pushed up premiums across all maturities, dealers said.
The six-month annualised forward premium closed Wednesday at 6.92 percent, up from the previous close.
The dollar supply was good and there was little demand from any other quarter, dealers said.
RBI had briefly suspended its dollar buying on March 31 when political uncertainty led to sharp volatility in the dollar-rupee spot market.
The rupee had slipped to 35.99 from 35.91/93 opening within minutes of trading on March 31 but quickly recovered and closed the day higher than the opening level.
The spot dollar closed at 35.865/870, a shade stronger compared to 35.875/895 opening, dealers said.
